results.evidence: normalize_query_for_write now has `else: normalized_query["uuid"] = str(uuid4())` when there is no existing_uuid, so a supplied uuid is overwritten. The rest of the query is copied via `dict(query)`.
`if existing_uuid: normalized_query["uuid"] = existing_uuid` is unchanged, and update_saved_metric still passes `existing_uuid=existing_uuid`.

`_move_inline_metrics_off_saved_metric_uuids` reads `update_data.get(metric_field, getattr(experiment, metric_field))` for both `metrics` and `metrics_secondary`. It compares each metric's uuid to `attached_saved_metric_uuids` (built from the payload's saved_metrics_ids) and sets `metric["uuid"] = str(uuid4())` on a match.
When nothing matches, `moved` is empty and `if not moved: continue` skips before update_data is touched. Stored inline metrics and ordering are not modified by this helper.

The helper only inserts the new uuid before the old one (`ordering.insert(position, new_uuid)`) and never removes the old one. It runs after both ordering syncs, so the shared metric's entry is already in the ordering. The old uuid therefore stays, with the new one beside it.
The helper only edits `update_data[metric_field]` and the ordering fields. The saved metric row and the saved_metrics_ids link sync are not touched.

The updated metric-configuration.md.j2 says to call `experiment-saved-metrics-create` "with its `query`". It then says to attach the shared metric and resend `metrics` without the inline entry in one update. It never tells the agent to omit the uuid when creating the shared metric. SKILL.md has no such instruction either.

`attached_saved_metric_uuids` is merged into `seen_metric_uuids`, so `_assign_uuids_to_metrics` regenerates a clashing resent inline uuid. The helper also covers `update_data` metrics. Ordering keeps the original uuid for the shared metric, per the code comment "the original uuid is kept on the incumbent".

+    @staticmethod
+    def _move_inline_metrics_off_saved_metric_uuids(
+        experiment: Experiment, update_data: dict, saved_metric_uuids: set[str]
+    ) -> None:
+        """Give a fresh uuid to every inline metric that shares one with an attached shared metric.
+
+        Dedup-on-input only covers the inline lists a write resends, so an update that changes just
+        the attached shared metrics never checks the stored ones. Attaching a shared metric promoted
+        from an inline metric would then leave both on the experiment under one uuid, and results,
+        matched by uuid, would show one metric's numbers on the other. The shared metric keeps its
+        uuid because every experiment using it references that one, so the inline copy moves.
+        """
+        if not saved_metric_uuids:
+            return
+
+        for metric_field, ordering_field in (
+            ("metrics", "primary_metrics_ordered_uuids"),
+            ("metrics_secondary", "secondary_metrics_ordered_uuids"),
+        ):
+            metrics = update_data.get(metric_field, getattr(experiment, metric_field, None))
+            if not metrics:
+                continue
+
+            moved: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
+            regenerated = deepcopy(metrics)
+            for metric in regenerated:
+                if not isinstance(metric, dict):
+                    continue
+                metric_uuid = metric.get("uuid")
+                if metric_uuid in saved_metric_uuids:
+                    metric["uuid"] = str(uuid4())
+                    moved.append((metric_uuid, metric["uuid"]))
+            if not moved:
+                continue
+
+            update_data[metric_field] = regenerated
+            ordering = list(update_data.get(ordering_field, getattr(experiment, ordering_field, None)) or [])
+            for old_uuid, new_uuid in moved:
+                # In front of the uuid it gave up, so the metric keeps its place in the list.
+                position = ordering.index(old_uuid) if old_uuid in ordering else len(ordering)
+                ordering.insert(position, new_uuid)
+            update_data[ordering_field] = ordering
+
